newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends down, gilts mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends down, gilts mixed.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday at 8.0 percent, off the day's high of 8.5 percent and dealers said they expected rates to ease further in the coming days.
They said call money was likely to ease on inflows into the banking system through interest payments on government securities and redemption of maturing stocks.
"Over the next two weeks, we should see around 10-15 billion rupees coming into the system from interest payments and redemptions," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
"The notified amounts at recent treasury bill auctions has come down from 5.0 billion rupees at the March 14 auction," he said.
"Each auction thereafter has been for less than 5.0 billion. So each week we should see some net inflow into banks from the bills which fall due for payment," the dealer said.
Dealers said prices of government securities were largely steady in moderate trade, with some stocks losing towards close.
They said market attention was focussed in stocks with maturities up to 2002.
"Towards the close of the day some primary dealers offloaded the 12.69 percent 2002 stock and it fell to 100.16 rupees from 100.25 yesterday," said a dealer.
"This also affected other stocks and the 13.50 percent 1997 stock fell to 101.88 from 101.92 earlier in the day and 101.95 yesterday," he said.

Among other active stocks, the 13.40 percent 1999 traded at 104.50 rupees against Monday's 104.49, the 13.80 percent 2002 rose to 105.65 from 105.60 while the 13.85 percemt 2001 rose to 104.85 from 104.70.
